game: CLE @ NE Week 8 2025, kickoff 2025-10-26 13:00 ET, Gillette outdoors

script.base: NE -7 at home, total 40.5, implied NE 23.8 / CLE 16.8. Patriots lead by the second half: Maye keeps the dropback game live early (Diggs 22 targets in weeks 5-7) then the clock goes to Stevenson (38 carries) with Maye already a designed/scramble runner (17/106). Cleveland is a Judkins offense (60 carries, 230 yards) because the dropback is broken (Jeudy 22 targets for 75 yards on 221 air; EPA/db -0.17 unblitzed, -0.38 vs blitz), so they run early and only tilt pass if the deficit grows. Not a shootout.
script.flip1: Grind stays inside one score. Judkins controls the clock against an NE run defense at 3.55 YPC, both passing games stay modest, Henderson never gets a featured series, and Diggs/Boutte do not need spike games.
script.flip2: NE blows it open early. Starter snaps get managed late, Stevenson grinds, Henderson can vulture garbage carries, and Cleveland abandons the run for empty dropbacks that still may not convert.

Usable negative overlap is the NE committee rushers into CLE's 3.50 YPC front.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both unders lost. Henderson rush+rec went over because NE led by 17 at half, Stevenson was rested, and Henderson took 12 garbage carries plus a screen to 55, or one 20-yard run turned the 36-yard template into 48 — the number only had 4.5 yards of room, and Huntington's concussion tag was the front getting thinner. Stevenson rec went over because Cleveland blitzed early, Maye threw two screens, and the 13-yard game from this same window repeated; 12.5 loses on one catch, and a season median on the number says the two zeros are not the whole role. Shared hole: these rungs may never have been real market prices, so the 'edge' is a median fade the books did not post.
slip_story: One story only: NE controls a 23.8-16.8 game, Stevenson is the closer so his receiving stays a non-role, and Henderson never becomes the rushing offense. Same-script stack, no TDs, one market per player. Do not add a game over, CLE pass overs, or Diggs/Boutte overs — those need the spike games and the NE secondary leak this slip is not built on. Do not add Stevenson rush over 18.5; the L3 mean is the 88-yard game.
